ops.title: durable.WriteFile's one-hour stump bound lets a crash loop accumulate full-binary temps
ops.description:
Found 2026-08-01 by the refuter on the program.go durable-write collapse, and it corrected a
justification I had accepted.

durable.WriteFile sweeps stale temps for the same target, bounded to those whose mtime is at least an
hour old, so a concurrent writer's in-flight temp is never unlinked. Measured consequence: six crash
iterations inside the hour, each followed by a real placement that writes, left **all six stumps** —
N crashes inside an hour leave N stumps that N intervening placements do not collect. At the program
call site each stump is up to a whole binary (10.9 MB measured).

The hand-rolled sweep this replaced was unbounded AND ran before os.CreateTemp, so it left at most
one stump and reclaimed the space before allocating the next full-size temp.

Two corrections to the reasoning that accepted the trade — both mine, both wrong:

1. I argued the mtime bound is "strictly stronger" than the lock-based safety it replaced, because
   the old sweep said nothing about a different consumer writing in the same shared root. False at
   this call site: a different consumer has a different Label, hence a different temp prefix, and the
   deleted sweep carried the identical prefix + dot-free-remainder rule. Different consumers' temps
   were already spared. The only case the bound adds is two writers of the SAME Label, which
   ensure.go's per-label start lock already serializes. So the sweep-timing regression was bought for
   nothing here.
2. The CHANGELOG claimed a stump "is collected by the next real placement". It is not, and the
   refuter corrected that text.

Bounded and self-healing (each stump goes after an hour), and it needs a crash in the narrow
CreateTemp-to-rename window, so this is not a merge blocker. But the bound is a durable/ design
question affecting every caller, not something to settle inside a collapse lane. Two directions: a
much shorter bound (a durable write takes milliseconds, so a minute would still protect any plausible
in-flight temp), or sweeping before CreateTemp so the space is reclaimed before it is needed — that
second one helps every caller and does not change the bound.

ops.text: A crash loop inside the stale window does not accumulate one stump per crash
A concurrent writer's in-flight temp is still never unlinked
